### I. SUBJECT MATTER

**Parties:** Dev Malik, Nila Sen

**Legal Category:** Criminal/Violent

**Brief Description:** Dev Malik allegedly assaulted Nila Sen by pushing her and blocking her exit. Both parties were injured. ### II. CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS ENGAGED

The following constitutional provisions are relevant to this matter:

- ****[PRIMARY]** Article 21 — Protection of Life and Personal Liberty**: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
  - Key principles: Right to life includes right to live with dignity, Right to a speedy trial, Right to health and medical care, Right to fair procedure, Right to safety and security, Due process and procedural fairness
- ****[PRIMARY]** Article 22 — Protection Against Arrest and Detention**: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds of arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. Every person detained under preventive detention must be informed of the grounds of detention.
  - Key principles: Right to be informed of grounds of arrest, Right to consult a lawyer, Safeguards against arbitrary detention, Preventive detention procedural safeguards
- ****[PRIMARY]** Article 20 — Protection in Respect of Conviction for Offences**: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the act. No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once. No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
  - Key principles: No ex post facto criminal law, No double jeopardy, Protection against self-incrimination

ipc_sections.title: Punishment for Voluntarily Causing Hurt
ipc_sections.offense_description: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine up to one thousand rupees.
ipc_sections.punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or Fine up to ₹1,000, or both
ipc_sections.inference_ground: Voluntarily causing bodily hurt to complainant

ipc_sections.title: Punishment for Voluntarily Causing Grievous Hurt
ipc_sections.offense_description: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_sections.inference_ground: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt resulting in severe injuries

ipc_sections.title: Punishment for Wrongful Restraint
ipc_sections.offense_description: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine up to five hundred rupees.
ipc_sections.punishment: Simple Imprisonment up to 1 month, or Fine up to ₹500, or both

ipc_sections.title: Assault or Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage Modesty
ipc_sections.offense_description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty.
ipc_sections.inference_ground: Assault or criminal force on woman

ipc_sections.title: Punishment for Criminal Intimidation
ipc_sections.offense_description: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment up to 2 years, or up to 7 years if threat is to cause death or grievous hurt.
ipc_sections.punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or up to 7 years + Fine (if threat of death)
